title: Circuit switching, packet switching
overview: Circuit switching reserves a dedicated end-to-end path before communication; packet switching divides a message into independently routed packets that share network links. You must compare both methods and explain the role of routers and packet headers.
syllabusPoints: Explain circuit switching, its advantages/disadvantages and suitable uses.
Explain packet switching, its advantages/disadvantages and suitable uses.
Explain the role of routers in packet-switched networks.
Describe how packets are routed and reassembled.

definitions.definition: A dedicated communication path is reserved for the duration of a session.
A message is divided into packets that independently share network routes.
A device that forwards packets between networks using destination information and routing data.
Control information carried with a packet, such as destination and sequencing information.

sections.title: Circuit switching
content: A route is established first and remains reserved. It can offer predictable latency/bandwidth, but capacity is wasted when the connection is idle, and failure of the reserved path can interrupt the session.

examples.label: Worked example
examples.content: Traditional real-time telephone networks are the classic example.

sections.title: Packet switching
content: A message is split into packets containing payload and control information. Packets may take different routes and arrive out of order; the destination uses sequence information to reconstruct the message. Missing/corrupt packets can be retransmitted.

sections.title: Why packet switching suits the internet
content: Many users share the same links efficiently, and routing can work around congestion or failed paths. The trade-offs are variable delay, header overhead and the need to reorder/retransmit packets.

sections.title: Routers
content: Each router examines destination information and selects a next hop using routing knowledge/tables. It does not need the entire message or one permanent end-to-end route.

comparisonTable.title: Switching methods compared
rows: Variable due to routing and queues

examTips: Compare the methods using the same criteria: reservation, delay, efficiency, failure handling and suitability.
State that packets can take different routes and be reassembled at the destination.
Do not claim packet switching guarantees fixed latency.
commonMistakes: Saying circuit switching sends packets along independently chosen routes.
Saying packets contain no addressing/control information.
Assuming routers rebuild the complete application message at every hop.
quickRecall: packets may arrive out of order
